title: Patient-level tests evaluate a quantum-inspired transformer model for breast ultrasound lesion classification
summary: A classical GAN/vision-transformer system jointly segmented breast-ultrasound lesions and classified malignancy in two public clinical-image datasets. The paper reports patient-level separation and bidirectional BUSI/UDIAT cross-dataset F1 scores of 97.14% and 96.81%. This is retrospective evaluation of existing images, and the authors state that actual clinical conditions were not reproduced. Larger heterogeneous clinical populations and prospective workflow evaluation are needed; the quantum-inspired components do not establish physical quantum computation or advantage.
ai_technology: Quantum-inspired generative adversarial segmentation with a vision-transformer classification head

evidence.tested: Patient-level validation on BUSI and UDIAT public breast-ultrasound image datasets, including cross-dataset testing in both directions; publisher reports cross-dataset F1 97.14% and 96.81%.
evidence.unknown: Prospective workflow performance, external validation by independent investigators, performance on larger and more heterogeneous populations, and clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: Learned GAN image segmentation and a ViT classification head were evaluated on held-out patient images; the source explicitly describes the quantum-inspired components as classical operations, not physical quantum computation.

source_review.scope: Publisher Article in Press PDF: dataset and patient-level split methods, architecture and learned operations, cross-dataset validation results, limitations and data-availability statement.
